questions.q: Why can self-attention parallelize across the sequence dimension during training while an RNN cannot?
options: Self-attention uses a smaller batch size
An RNN's hidden state at step t depends on step t-1, a strict sequential chain; self-attention computes every position's relevance to every other position in one batched matmul
RNNs are not supported on GPUs at all
Self-attention does not use matrix multiplication
questions.explain: The RNN recurrence forces step-by-step computation; self-attention has no such dependency and computes all pairwise relevance scores in a single batched operation.

questions.q: What is meant by 'path length' between two positions in a sequence model?
options: The physical distance between GPU cores
The number of computational steps information must travel to get from one position to another
The number of layers in the model
The length of the input sequence in characters
questions.explain: Path length measures how many computational hops are needed for information at one position to influence another -- O(n) for an RNN, O(1) for self-attention.

questions.q: How does self-attention's path length between any two positions compare to an RNN's?
options: Self-attention: O(n); RNN: O(1)
Self-attention: O(1); RNN: O(n)
Both are O(n^2)
Both are O(1)
questions.explain: Self-attention connects any two positions directly through one computation (O(1)), while an RNN's information must pass through every intermediate hidden state (O(n)).

questions.q: What cost does self-attention accept in exchange for parallelism and O(1) path length?
options: It requires no backpropagation
Its compute and memory scale as O(n^2) with sequence length, compared to an RNN's O(n)
It cannot be used with GPUs
It eliminates the need for positional encoding
questions.explain: Because every position attends to every other position, self-attention's cost grows quadratically with sequence length, a real trade-off against the RNN's linear cost.

questions.q: Why does a shorter path length between positions help with long-range dependencies?
options: It doesn't -- path length is unrelated to long-range dependencies
Fewer computational steps between two positions means less opportunity for signal (and gradient) to vanish along the way
Shorter path length only matters for short sequences
It reduces the vocabulary size needed
questions.explain: Each step along a long path is another chance for the vanishing-gradient problem to erase signal; a direct, O(1) connection avoids that entirely.
